messages.content:
Three ants walk on a thin rod 100 cm long.
When an ant reaches either end of the rod it falls off. When two ants meet,
they BOUNCE: both instantly reverse direction, and each keeps its own speed.

Starting positions and velocities (positive = toward the 100 cm end):

- Ant A: at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s
- Ant B: at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s
- Ant C: at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s

After how many seconds does the LAST ant fall off the rod? Give the exact
number of seconds.


When you are finished, output your final answer on its own line, as the last line of your response, in the exact format:
ANSWER: <your answer>

text:
We can treat each ant as passing through the others without bouncing, because the bounce is equivalent to them swapping identities.  

The times for each ant to fall if they walked straight without collisions:

- Ant A: starts at 10 cm, moving +3 cm/s.  
  Distance to right end = 90 cm. Time = \( 90 / 3 = 30 \) seconds.  
  Distance to left end = 10 cm. Time = \( 10 / 3 \approx 3.33 \) s, but it's moving right, so it will hit right end first.

- Ant B: starts at 40 cm, moving -1 cm/s.  
  Distance to left end = 40 cm. Time = \( 40 / 1 = 40 \) seconds.  
  Distance to right end = 60 cm, but it's moving left, so left end is relevant.

- Ant C: starts at 80 cm, moving -2 cm/s.  
  Distance to left end = 80 cm. Time = \( 80 / 2 = 40 \) seconds.  
  Distance to right end = 20 cm, but moving left.

Under the identity-swapping interpretation, the last ant to fall corresponds to the longest of these straight-line times.  

Times: A = 30 s, B = 40 s, C = 40 s.  
The last ant falls at 40 seconds.

ANSWER: 40
